options: Deleting data that is no longer used
The collection and evaluation of data from various sources, often to understand trends and patterns
Assigning access rights to database tables
Splitting a dataset into training and testing subsets
Selling data to third parties
questions.explanation: Data Discovery involves the collection and evaluation of data from various sources and is often used to understand trends and patterns in the data.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT one of the data problems listed as reasons why raw source data must be streamlined before Data Discovery results reach end users?
options: Null values
Different date formats
Spelling mistakes and special characters
Different codes for the same product across systems
Data stored in more than one language
questions.explanation: The listed problems are nulls, differing date formats, spelling mistakes, special characters, different product codes and duplicates; multiple languages are not mentioned.

questions.stem: In the Data Discovery example, a Glass product is coded GLS in one source system and GS in another. What problem does this illustrate?
options: Different codes for the same product across source systems
Null values in the product table
Duplicate rows in one system
Special characters in product names
Different date formats
questions.explanation: The Glass code being GLS in one system and GS in another illustrates that data can have different codes for the same product.

questions.stem: Which group mostly prefers raw data without any cleaning, cleansing or scrubbing, for use in Data Dredging, Snooping, p-hacking and Fishing?
options: Business end users
C-level executives
Data Scientists
Data Analysts
Finance consultants
questions.explanation: Data Scientists mostly prefer raw data without cleaning, cleansing or scrubbing so they can use techniques such as Data Dredging, Snooping, p-hacking and Fishing.

questions.stem: What state of data do Data Analysts mostly prefer for Data Discovery?
options: Completely raw data
Data that is encrypted
Data that has been fully scrubbed, wrangled and munged
Data that has at least been cleaned and cleansed
Data that has been aggregated into KPIs only
questions.explanation: Data Analysts mostly prefer data after it has at least been cleaned and cleansed.

questions.stem: What do Business End Users and C-level executives expect of data before it reaches them for decision making?
options: That it is raw, so they can explore it themselves
That it is cleaned, cleansed, scrubbed, wrangled and munged
That it is only cleaned
That it is stored in a Data Lake
That it is delivered as a spreadsheet
questions.explanation: Business End Users and C-level expect data to be cleaned, cleansed, scrubbed, wrangled and munged before it reaches them, which the author calls a fair expectation.

questions.stem: How does Data Discovery differ across roles?
options: It is identical for every role in the organisation
It only applies to Data Scientists
It only applies to C-level executives
It applies only to IT staff
It is different for Data Scientists, Data Analysts, Business End Users and C-level
questions.explanation: Data Discovery is different for different roles, namely Data Scientists, Data Analysts, Business End Users and C-level.

questions.stem: With which discipline is Data Discovery usually associated?
options: Business Intelligence
Network security
Software testing
Payroll processing
Physical data modelling
questions.explanation: Data Discovery is usually associated with Business Intelligence and helps inform business decisions.

questions.stem: How does Data Discovery help inform business decisions?
options: By deleting siloed data sources
By restricting analysis to a single source
By bringing together disparate, siloed data sources to be analysed
By replacing analysis with intuition
By outsourcing analysis to consultants
questions.explanation: Data Discovery helps inform business decisions by bringing together disparate, siloed data sources so they can be analysed.

questions.stem: Why can understanding trends and patterns NOT simply be done on data straight from source systems?
options: Because source systems are always offline
Because trends only exist in Data Lakes
Because end users are not allowed to see source data
Because source data can contain nulls, inconsistent formats, mistakes, differing codes and duplicates that must be streamlined first
Because source data is always encrypted
questions.explanation: Source data can have null values, different date formats, spelling mistakes, special characters, different codes for the same product and duplicates, so it must be streamlined before it is presented to end users.
